title: Moussaka
subtitle: Greek baked lamb and aubergine with bechamel
excerpt: The great Greek baked dish: layers of roasted aubergine, a rich cinnamon-spiced lamb and tomato sauce, and a thick, nutmeg-scented bechamel crust, baked until golden and set into a firm, sliceable gratin. A dish that takes time but makes excellent leftovers.

recipe.sourceNotes: Moussaka is the most internationally recognised Greek dish and one of the great gratins of the Mediterranean. The modern Greek version was refined by Nikolaos Tselementes, the influential Greek chef and cookery writer, who published a systematised version in the 1930s that added the bechamel topping (which he modelled on the French béchamel), giving the dish its now-canonical form. Before Tselementes, Greek moussaka was closer to the layered aubergine and meat dishes still made across the Middle East (like Arab musaqa'a) without the cream sauce. The dish also exists in Turkish (musakka) and Levantine versions. The defining elements of the Greek version are the aubergine layers (often fried but better roasted for less oil), the lamb mince sauce with cinnamon and allspice, and the thick bechamel set with egg so it slices cleanly.

recipeTools.notes: A deep 30 x 20 cm baking tin.

content.text: Roasting the aubergine rather than frying uses less oil and produces a better result for the final dish. Salt the aubergine slices and leave for 20 minutes to draw out moisture, then rinse and dry before roasting. The bechamel must be thick; add the egg yolks after it cools slightly so they do not scramble. Allow the assembled dish to cool for at least 20 minutes before cutting.

items.preparation: sliced 1 cm thick; salted, rinsed, and dried

content.text: Lay the aubergine slices on baking trays, brush with 3 tablespoons of olive oil, and season. Roast at 200 C (180 C fan) for 20 to 25 minutes, turning once, until golden. Set aside. Make the meat sauce: brown the lamb mince in batches in the remaining oil. Fry the onion until soft. Add the garlic, cinnamon, allspice, and oregano. Add the tomatoes and simmer for 20 minutes until thick. Season.

Make the bechamel: melt the butter, add the flour, and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the warm milk until smooth and thick. Cook for 5 minutes. Season with nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Remove from the heat, cool for 5 minutes, then beat in the egg yolks.

Layer half the aubergine slices in a 30 x 20 cm baking tin. Cover with all the meat sauce. Layer the remaining aubergine on top. Pour the bechamel evenly over the top. Scatter with parmesan. Bake at 180 C (160 C fan) for 45 minutes until golden and set. Cool for 20 minutes before cutting.
